name: p4-0308-ratelimit-atomicfile
title: Token Bucket Rate Limiting and Atomic POSIX File Replacement
anchor: ### 3.5 Rate limits, concurrency and file operations
spec: Two side-by-side architectural diagrams. Left panel 'Outbound Rate Limiting (Token Bucket)': A bucket container labeled 'Capacity B tokens' has tokens dropping in from a tap at 'Refill rate: r tokens/sec'. Client requests enter from the top; when a token is present, a token is consumed and the request proceeds to the fleet endpoint with headers 'X-RateLimit-Remaining: N'. If the bucket is empty, the request queues or yields until the next token drops. An error branch shows HTTP 429 Too Many Requests leading to a pause respecting 'Retry-After: 30'. Right panel 'Atomic File Updates vs TOCTOU Race Condition': Upper bad path 'Unsafe Check-Then-Open' shows Step 1 'if exists(config.json)' followed by a time gap (window of vulnerability) where a concurrent agent or crash causes a race, resulting in 'Corrupted / Partial Read' or FileNotFoundError. Lower good path 'Atomic POSIX Replace' shows: Step 1 'Write full payload to temporary file in same directory (.config.json.tmp)' ensuring identical filesystem/mount point. Step 2 'Flush and close'. Step 3 'os.replace(.config.json.tmp, config.json)' executing an atomic directory inode pointer update. Step 4 'Mutual Exclusion' note highlighting 'fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)' and 'open with os.O_EXCL' preventing concurrent overwrite.
alt: A token bucket rate limiter handing out tokens alongside safe atomic file replacement using temporary files and os.replace compared to an unsafe TOCTOU race condition.
cap: Outbound rate limiting uses a token bucket to avoid 429 errors, while safe file state updates require writing to a sibling temporary file before an atomic os.replace.
